problem_statement:
Resetting primary key for a child model doesn't work.
Description
	
In the attached example code setting the primary key to None does not work (so that the existing object is overwritten on save()).
The most important code fragments of the bug example:
from django.db import models
class Item(models.Model):
	# uid = models.UUIDField(primary_key=True, default=uuid.uuid4, editable=False)
	uid = models.AutoField(primary_key=True, editable=False)
	f = models.BooleanField(default=False)
	def reset(self):
		self.uid = None
		self.f = False
class Derived(Item):
	pass
class SaveTestCase(TestCase):
	def setUp(self):
		self.derived = Derived.objects.create(f=True) # create the first object
		item = Item.objects.get(pk=self.derived.pk)
		obj1 = item.derived
		obj1.reset()
		obj1.save() # the first object is overwritten
	def test_f_true(self):
		obj = Item.objects.get(pk=self.derived.pk)
		self.assertTrue(obj.f)
Django 2.1.2

+                        setattr(self, parent._meta.pk.attname, getattr(self, field.attname))
+                else:
+                    # Existing instance with a reset parent pk: clear the parent link, too.
+                    setattr(self, field.attname, None)

reviewer_reasoning: The bug occurs because, for multi-table inheritance, saving a child with parent.pk set to None re-synchronizes the parent pk from the existing parent-link field, causing an UPDATE of the original row instead of an INSERT. The patch changes the sync logic: when not adding and the parent pk is None, it clears the parent link field too, preventing the pk from being repopulated and letting the save path treat it as an insert. It preserves the original behavior for new instances (adding=True) by still copying an existing parent link into the parent pk. This directly addresses the reported case so the original object isn’t overwritten and a new one is created instead.
